claim: The tracer particles are excited at 620 nm, as specified by the supplier for the product family.
validity_conditions: As with the emission peak, a band reported as a point: no width is printed, so none is asserted. Diameter-independent. WHETHER THIS LINE CAN ACTUALLY BE DELIVERED IS A SEPARATE QUESTION and is not answered here -- which light engine reaches the sample, and at what wavelength, lives in kb/staging/devices.v0.json under light_engines, and the lapp_branch_assignment gap there is still open. A tracer that is excitable at 620 nm and an instrument that can excite it are two facts, and only the first is on this data sheet. THE PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION IS WITHDRAWN -- THIS ENTRY IS NOT ABOUT THE BOTTLE ON THIS BENCH. On 2026-09-19 the person ruled that AFR-0500-COOH is not what is in use. Two facts force it: the bottle's label does not state a product identity (bottle_label_states_no_product, E3, and it was LOOKED AT -- so this is permanent doubt, not doubt pending a look), and the particles in use fluoresce under green excitation and show through a 605 band (particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, E2), which a particle emitting at 680 nm as this data sheet specifies does not do. The observation was made on this bench and the specification was not; 10.3 rule 1 binds a vendor exactly as it binds a prior project. WHAT IS AND IS NOT RETRACTED. This entry remains TRUE ABOUT THE ABVIGEN PRODUCT. Nothing in the data sheet has been found wrong about the thing the data sheet describes. What is withdrawn is that the thing it describes is ours. It is kept rather than deleted under rule 8, and because the next person to find this sheet needs to meet the record that it was examined and set aside. THE QUERY HANDLES WERE RENAMED, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL REPAIR. The numbers used to answer to names beginning `tracer_`, and the word `tracer` is the claim that these are ours -- asserted in a string that nothing validates. Check 44 refused the `subject` fields on these entries and they were removed rather than gamed, which left the name as the only handle, so the claim did not disappear when the check rejected it: it moved somewhere no check reaches. The names now begin `abvigen_`, so a query for our tracer no longer lands here. The entry_id still begins `tracer_` and is deliberately left alone: it is the citation handle, it is referenced by name from the polystyrene dispersion entries, and renaming it would be a deletion under rule 8. A FOOTNOTE THAT IS REALLY THE WHOLE LESSON: renaming the number left this entry's `subject` dangling, and check 44 caught it immediately. The subject had been resolving only because a number in this same file carried the same name -- the entry was its own registry. That is the self-assertion manager-librarian named: a name that asserts its own subject is a subject nothing can refuse. The id is updated to match rather than removed, because consistency is the most that can be done inside this store; what would actually fix it is a registry for the sample, which does not exist and is raised.
